definitions.explanation: The most abbreviated and flowing style of Chinese/Japanese calligraphy. Characters are highly simplified and strokes are often connected, making it difficult to read without specialized training.

examples.japanese: {草書|そうしょ}は{読|よ}みにくい。
examples.english: Cursive script is hard to read.

examples.japanese: {草書|そうしょ}で{書|か}かれた{手紙|てがみ}を{解読|かいどく}する。
examples.english: To decipher a letter written in cursive script.

examples.japanese: ひらがなは{漢字|かんじ}の{草書|そうしょ}{体|たい}から{生|う}まれた{文字|もじ}だ。
examples.english: Hiragana are characters that evolved from the cursive forms of Chinese characters.

notes: Composed of {草|そう} (grass, rough draft) + {書|しょ} (writing, script). Also called {草書体|そうしょたい}. The most abbreviated of the five script styles. Key historical fact: Japanese hiragana developed from {草書|そうしょ} forms of {万葉仮名|まんようがな} characters — for example, あ derives from the {草書|そうしょ} of {安|あん}, and は from {波|は}. Common collocations: {草書|そうしょ}{体|たい} (cursive style), {草書|そうしょ}で{書|か}く (to write in cursive). While rarely used in modern daily life, {草書|そうしょ} remains important in {書道|しょどう} (calligraphy) and for reading historical documents.
